subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Ratchets: Motion That Won't Go Back
description: A quick win: understand Ratchets: Motion That Won't Go Back.

hook.text: A socket wrench clicks as you turn it. It grips in one direction and slips in the other.

buildup.text: A ratchet uses a pawl — a small lever that catches on angled teeth. It allows rotation one way only.

discovery.text: Wind-up watches use ratchets. The crown winds the mainspring, and the ratchet prevents it from unwinding.

twist.text: Zip ties are linear ratchets. The ridges lock the strap tighter and tighter. No going back.

climax.text: Ratchets secure cargo straps, jack stands, and roller coaster lift chains. One-way motion saves lives.

punchline.text: Forward only. The ratchet makes retreat impossible.

quiz.question: What component in a ratchet mechanism prevents backward motion?
options: A friction pad that grips the gear teeth when reversed
A pawl that catches on angled teeth in one direction only
A spring that pushes the gear forward continuously
